chunks.text: Find the deadline. You have five seconds.
Missed it? It was here, in the third paragraph.
Now the easy-language version.
There. In the first sentence.
At least 844,000 adults in Switzerland struggle with reading.
Letters like this decide their money, their deadlines, their rights.
No one should be shut out.
But easy-language versions are slow expert work.
Leicht·Facile drafts them with Apertus, the Swiss open model.
The writers get a checked first draft.
Apertus reads the letter the way you just tried to, and writes down every answer: what to do, by when, what it costs, whom to ask.
Then it writes the draft.
Code checks every date, amount and phone number, and 45 easy-language rules, in milliseconds.
A larger Apertus model judges the meaning; only flagged sentences are repaired.
Every sentence links to its source. The writer approves each one.
A strong single prompt, in its default mode, lost almost a quarter of the hard facts, without a word.
Leicht·Facile lists every one it misses.
Patient letters, child protection decisions, tax letters:
under secrecy, they may not go to a foreign cloud.
Closed models stay with their makers.
Most open models keep their training data closed.
Most fully open ones are built abroad.
Apertus is open down to its data, built and trained in Switzerland, and runs in-house.
Ticino already runs it for sensitive documents.
For these letters, it is the only option.
